package middleware

	"net/http"

func TestTmpBalancerEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	e := echo.New()
	c := e.NewContext(httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil), httptest.NewRecorder())

	rb := NewRandomBalancer(nil)
	assert.Nil(t, rb.Next(c))

	rrb := NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{})
	assert.Nil(t, rrb.Next(c))

	// middleware must not panic and should respond 503
	e2 := echo.New()
	e2.Use(Proxy(NewRandomBalancer(nil)))
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	e2.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil))
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, rec.Code)

	e3 := echo.New()
	e3.Use(Proxy(NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil)))
	rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
	e3.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil))
	assert.Equal(t, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, rec.Code)
}
EOF

Fixed in middleware/proxy.go:

- `randomBalancer.Next` now returns `nil` when the target list is empty (instead of calling `rand.Intn(0)`, which panics with "invalid argument to Intn").
- `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now returns `nil` when the target list is empty (instead of `i % 0`, which panics with "integer divide by zero").
- `ProxyWithConfig` now handles a `nil` target from the balancer by returning `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) instead of dereferencing a nil target and panicking.

Verified: `rb.Next(c)` and `rrb.Next(c)` both return nil for empty/nil target lists, the middleware responds 503 with no targets, and the full suite (`go test ./...`) passes.

arguments.text: Fixed in router.go: `Router.Find` no longer sets `ctx.path` to the request path up front; the path is now only set to the matched route's registered path (currentNode.ppath). So for a request that matches no route, `c.Path()` is "" (as documented: "Path returns the registered path for the handler"), while matched routes and 405s still report their route path. Verified with a test reproducing your snippet and the full suite passes.

Fixed in context.go: `Scheme()` now only accepts a header value that is actually a valid HTTP scheme (`http`/`https`) — matching its documented contract ("Scheme returns the HTTP protocol scheme, `http` or `https`"). Bogus values such as `ftp` are ignored and the next fallback is used (X-Forwarded-Proto → X-Forwarded-Protocol → X-Forwarded-Ssl → X-Url-Scheme), defaulting to "http" when nothing valid is present. Your snippet now prints "https". Full suite passes.

Fixed in bind.go: `bindData` now supports the documented map destinations — `map[string][]string` (all values per key, no more panic), `map[string]string` (first value), and `map[string]interface{}` (the full []string value). `?tag=a&tag=b` into `map[string][]string` now yields `{"tag": ["a","b"]}`, and `map[string]interface{}` holds the slice. Full suite passes.

Fixed in group.go/echo.go/router.go: `Group.Use` no longer registers catch-all `Any("", …)`/`Any("/*", …)` routes (which overwrote the GET handler of the first group sharing the prefix). It now uses a dedicated pseudo-method `RouteNotFound` (`Echo#RouteNotFound` / `Group#RouteNotFound`, constant `echo.RouteNotFound`), consulted by the router only when no route/method matched. So `GET /group` runs `h` with `m1` and `GET /group/other` runs `h` with `m2`, while group middleware still runs for unmatched paths inside the group (404). Full suite passes.

Fixed in middleware/compress.go: the gzip middleware no longer strips `Content-Encoding: gzip` for an empty body when the response is already committed (the gzip header bytes are already on the wire, so removing the header produced a body that was gzip data but not advertised as such). Now `c.String(200, "")` with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` returns `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8` and a valid gzip stream that decompresses to an empty body. The uncommitted cases (errors, 204 No Content) still drop the header and stay uncompressed. Full suite passes.
